categories.name: build
why: P2 because it changes how Bitcoin Core is built on a supported platform, with benchmarked ~35-55% faster block validation and ~40% faster CI builds when using clang-cl versus MSVC.
It also removes recurring MSVC internal-compiler-error workarounds that have cost maintainer time, a stated motivation from the author and echoed by maflcko.
Not urgent (no current build is broken) but durable value worth deliberate review.

result.summary: This PR switches the native Windows build (via CMake presets and CI) from MSVC (cl.exe) to Clang's clang-cl.exe, and ultimately drops MSVC support entirely after extensive discussion. It adjusts diagnostic flags, links the clang builtins library for __int128 division, fixes a few compiler-specific quirks (BSWAP_CONSTEXPR, shlwapi linking, leveldb warnings), and adds release notes and doc updates for the new toolchain.
result.problem: MSVC lacks inline assembly support on x64/ARM64 (precluding some hardware-accelerated code paths) and has repeatedly caused internal-compiler-error maintenance overhead; this affects Windows developers and anyone building Bitcoin Core natively on Windows.

open_concerns: maflcko (2026-08-18): whether the -Wno-return-type suppression around missing-switch-case + assert(false) hides real undefined behavior; unanswered since then.
hodlinator: whether doc/build-windows-msvc.md should be renamed, and whether an obsolete #elif branch in byteswap.h should be removed now that MSVC is dropped.

fanquake earlier flagged the CMake logic mixing if(MSVC) and if(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID STREQUAL "MSVC") as fragile/confusing; addressed by explanation but not fully resolved to fanquake's satisfaction.

fanquake's netaddress.h placement question was addressed by moving code to compat.h.
Various CI/link warnings raised by fanquake and maflcko (unused-private-field, missing-braces, shlwapi overlinking) were investigated and fixed.

Benchmark numbers are self-reported by the author on their own machine and not independently reproduced by other reviewers.
result.card: This PR switches Bitcoin Core's native Windows build from MSVC (cl.exe) to Clang (clang-cl.exe) and, after sustained maintainer pushback, ultimately drops MSVC support entirely. The stated motivation is MSVC's lack of inline-assembly support on x64/ARM64 and recurring internal-compiler-error maintenance costs; the author also posted benchmarks showing clang-cl producing roughly 35-55% faster block validation and ~40% faster CI builds than MSVC. Review has been extensive over more than a year (35 force-pushes) with concept ACKs from fanquake and hodlinator once MSVC removal was agreed to, but a concern raised by maflcko on 2026-08-18 about whether a warning suppression might be hiding real undefined behavior on Windows remains unanswered by the author. The PR is otherwise well reviewed and touches CMake build configuration, CI scripts, and a few compiler-compatibility fixes in shared code, with no dependency blocking it other than already-merged rebases.
